fullPassage:
[1번] One day, my father took me and my brother on a camping trip. While driving to a nearby forest, he explained how to set up the tent. Almost immediately after we arrived, however, my brother was stung by a wasp, which caused his forehead to swell. We tried to catch our dinner by fishing in a nearby lake, but we failed miserably, returning with nothing but dozens of mosquito bites. Without any fish, we cooked a can of beans over a campfire, which was an unwise endeavor that burned the bottom layer of beans while leaving those on top cold. When bedtime came, we unrolled my father's old sleeping bags to find them stinking of damp mold. The odor was so overpowering that even my father gave up. We packed the tent, got in the car, and drove home.

[2번] The Venus flytrap, a meat-eating plant, has a pair of leaves that act as jaws and a stomach. If an insect touches the trigger hairs on the surface of these leaves, the leaves close, trapping the insect. Amazingly, a recent experiment showed that the Venus flytrap knew how many times its trigger hairs were touched and could even count the time between these stimuli. The trap closed only if the plant sensed two stimuli within a 20 second time span. Once 20 seconds passed, the process was reset. In addition, more than three stimuli were required for the plant to begin producing the enzymes that digest the trapped insect. Thanks to this process, the Venus flytrap doesn't make meaningless efforts trying to trap and digest raindrops or fallen leaves.

[3번] The "Rat Park" was an experiment conducted by a psychologist in the late 1970s. It was used to show that a social community can be more powerful than drugs. In the experiment, rats were given a choice between two bottles, one containing plain water and the other containing water with morphine added to it. The psychologist found that rats kept together drank much less of the morphine water than rats kept alone. He concluded that addictive qualities aren't the only thing that promotes drug use. The social and environmental conditions of the individual also play an important role. This seems to apply to humans as well as rats. People who are lonely and isolated are more likely to become addicted to drugs. But if these conditions are improved, their chances of breaking the addiction increase. This means that social recovery could someday become a treatment for drug addiction.

[4번] "Negative pressure" refers to a situation in which the pressure of an enclosed area is lower than that of the surrounding area. If the barrier between these two areas breaks, any substances in the high-pressure area will immediately flow into the low-pressure area. For example, undersea pipes used to transport oil are in a state of negative pressure; therefore, any break in the pipeline will cause it to fill with ocean water. This is much better than the opposite scenario, in which oil would be released into the ocean. However, negative pressure is not always beneficial, such as in the case of pipes carrying drinking water to a city. If these municipal waterlines are damaged, they can potentially suck in contaminated groundwater, which would then enter the water supply. For this reason, a system of gauges and valves is used to adjust and control their pressure.

[5번] If astronauts travel to Mars in the near future, the journey will probably take years. Therefore, providing the astronauts with enough to eat will be a major challenge. Scientists are now looking for ways to allow astronauts to extend their food supply by growing crops. Seeds take up less storage space than packaged meals, and astronauts can plant them once they reach Mars. NASA is already conducting experiments to find out what might grow on Mars. The soil on Mars is made up mostly of crushed rocks, so it has few or no nutrients. In a test, NASA planted lettuce in crushed volcanic rock from Hawaii, which also contains few nutrients. The lettuce took a long time to grow, but it tasted normal. Because this test was a success, NASA now plans to find out how long other vegetables would take to grow on Mars.

[6번] Every four years, a twenty-ninth day is added to the month of February. This day, also known as Leap Day, was created to ensure that our calendar and our seasons stay in line with each other. While we think that a normal year consists of 365 days, it actually takes Earth about 365.2421 days to orbit the sun. Every four years, it is necessary to add an extra day to account for the lost time. Without the addition of a leap day, winter would occur earlier in the calendar year, causing problems for agricultural schedules and potentially leading to crop failures. Additionally, many holidays and cultural celebrations are linked to specific seasons or dates. Without leap years to keep the calendar in check, these events would gradually drift away from their intended time of celebration.

[7번] The urgency instinct is what allows people to act quickly when faced with danger. It is particularly useful in emergency situations, where making quick decisions is essential. However, in non-emergency situations, it can cause people to panic and make poor decisions. One example of the urgency instinct in mass media is the fear of terrorism. People in the Western world fear terrorism more than heart disease, despite the fact that heart disease represents a much greater threat. The reason for this is the media's coverage of terrorist attacks, which greatly exaggerates the threat of terrorism. In reality, the possibility of being killed in a terrorist attack is extremely low. The chances of dying from heart disease, on the other hand, are much higher. The urgency instinct causes us to feel that immediate action is required to combat terrorism, even though there are many more significant threats. This is why rational analysis is required. It allows us to counteract the urgency instinct and respond to risks accordingly.

[8번] In 2011, Joao Pereira de Souza, an old man living in an island village near Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, found a penguin struggling on the beach. The helpless, starving creature covered in oil was adopted by Mr. de Souza and named Dindim. Mr. de Souza nursed him back to health and released him, thinking they would never meet again. Amazingly, though, Dindim returned! It is believed that he traveled around 5,000 miles between Mr. de Souza's house and the coasts of Argentina and Chile. What is more, he makes this journey every year. After spending about eight months with Mr. de Souza, he goes on his annual migration for his breeding routine, only to return once again.

det.korean: such → so (so + 형용사 + that: 너무 ~해서 …하다)

det.korean: 정답 ④ produce → producing: begin은 뒤에 동명사(-ing)나 to부정사를 취해요. 동사원형(produce)은 바로 올 수 없어요.

② closed: 'The trap closed(그 덫이 닫혔다)'로 과거시제가 맞아요. (정상)

det.korean: 정답 ③ knows → knew: 앞 동사 showed가 과거예요. 그래서 뒤에 오는 동사도 과거(knew)로 시제를 맞춰야 해요.
det.analysis:

② close: 'the leaves close(잎들이 닫히다)'에서 주어 the leaves가 복수라 -s가 없는 close가 맞아요. (정상)

④ were required: 주어 more than three stimuli(세 번보다 많은 자극)가 복수라서 were가 맞고, '자극이 요구되다'라는 수동의 뜻이라 required가 맞아요. (정상)

② reach: 'once they reach Mars' 현재시제 — 적절
③ made: 'is made up of' 수동태(be + 과거분사) — 적절
④ would: 'how long...would take' — 적절
det.tip: '~하는 것'이 주어일 때는 동사에 -ing를 붙여요. provide(X) → providing(O)

questions.passage: Every four years, a twenty-ninth day is added to the month of February. This day, also known as Leap Day, was ①<u>created</u> to ensure that our calendar and our seasons stay in line with each other. While we think that a normal year consists of 365 days, it actually takes Earth about 365.2421 days to ②<u>escape</u> the sun. Every four years, it is necessary to add an extra day to account for the lost time. Without the addition of a leap day, winter would ③<u>occur</u> earlier in the calendar year, causing problems for agricultural schedules and potentially leading to crop failures. Additionally, many holidays and cultural celebrations are linked to specific seasons or dates. Without leap years to keep the calendar in check, these events would gradually ④<u>drift</u> away from their intended time of celebration.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② escape → orbit이 맞아요. 지구가 태양을 '공전하는(orbit)' 데 걸리는 시간을 말하는데 escape(탈출하다)로 바뀌어 문맥이 어긋나요.
det.analysis:
① created: 윤일이 달력을 맞추려고 '만들어졌다' — 문맥상 적절해요.

② escape: it takes Earth about 365.2421 days to ___ the sun — 지구가 태양을 '공전하는(orbit)' 시간이어야 하는데 escape(탈출하다)로 바뀌어 어색해요. ←정답

③ occur: winter would occur earlier(겨울이 더 일찍 온다) — 적절해요.

④ drift: events would drift away(행사들이 벗어난다) — 적절해요.
det.tip: orbit the sun = 태양을 공전하다. escape(탈출)와는 정반대 느낌이에요.

questions.passage: The urgency instinct is what allows people to act quickly when faced with danger. It is particularly useful in emergency situations, where making quick decisions is essential. However, in non-emergency situations, it can cause people to panic and make poor decisions. One example of the urgency instinct in mass media is the fear of terrorism. People in the Western world fear terrorism more than heart disease, despite the fact that heart disease represents a much greater threat. The reason for this is the media's coverage of terrorist attacks, which greatly exaggerates the threat of terrorism. In reality, the possibility of being killed in a terrorist attack is extremely low. The chances of dying from heart disease, on the other hand, are much higher. The urgency instinct causes us to feel that immediate action is required to combat terrorism, even though there are many more significant threats. This is why rational analysis is required. It allows us to counteract the urgency instinct and respond to risks accordingly.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ④ 위급하지 않은 상황에서 긴급 본능이 공황·잘못된 판단 유발 — 일치
det.analysis:
① 심장병을 더 두려워한다: 본문은 서구 사람들이 '테러를 더 두려워한다(fear terrorism more than heart disease)'고 했어요. 반대라 불일치.

② 항상 올바른 판단: 위급하지 않은 상황에서는 '잘못된 판단(poor decisions)'을 부른다고 했어요. 불일치.

③ 테러 사망 가능성이 더 크다: 테러는 '낮고' 심장병이 '높다'고 했어요. 반대라 불일치.

④ 공황·잘못된 판단: 'in non-emergency situations, it can cause people to panic and make poor decisions'와 일치해요. ←정답
det.tip: 테러를 더 두려워함, 위급하지 않을 땐 poor decisions — 이 둘을 뒤집은 오답 주의.

ch: 서구 사람들은 테러보다 심장병을 더 두려워한다.
긴급 본능은 어떤 상황에서도 항상 올바른 판단을 낳는다.
테러로 인한 사망 가능성이 심장병으로 인한 것보다 크다.
위급하지 않은 상황에서는 긴급 본능이 공황과 잘못된 판단을 낳을 수 있다.

questions.passage: In 2011, Joao Pereira de Souza, an old man living in an island village near Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, ①<u>found</u> a penguin struggling on the beach. The helpless, starving creature covered in oil was adopted by Mr. de Souza and named Dindim. Mr. de Souza nursed him back to health and ②<u>releasing</u> him, thinking they would never meet again. Amazingly, though, Dindim returned! It is ③<u>believed</u> that he traveled around 5,000 miles between Mr. de Souza's house and the coasts of Argentina and Chile. What is more, he makes this journey every year. After spending about eight months with Mr. de Souza, he goes on his annual migration for his breeding routine, only to ④<u>return</u> once again.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① found=발견했다(과거) ② releasing→released(과거, 병렬) ③ believed=여겨지는(수동) ④ return=돌아오다(to부정사)
det.analysis:
① found: 2011년에 발견했다 — 과거시제 적절
② releasing: 'nursed him back to health and ___ him'에서 앞의 nursed(과거동사)와 and로 연결된 병렬이므로 같은 과거동사 released가 필요. releasing(분사)은 틀림 ←정답
③ believed: 'It is believed' 수동태 — 적절
④ return: 'only to return'은 결과의 to부정사(to+동사원형) — 적절
det.tip: A and B 병렬: nursed(과거) and released(과거). releasing(분사)은 짝이 안 맞음

questions.passage: One day, my father took me and my brother on a camping trip. While driving to a nearby forest, he explained how to set up the tent. Almost immediately after we arrived, however, my brother was stung by a wasp, which caused his forehead to ①<u>swell</u>. We tried to catch our ②<u>dinner</u> by fishing in a nearby lake, but we failed miserably, returning with nothing but dozens of mosquito bites. Without any fish, we cooked a can of ③<u>beans</u> over a campfire, which was an unwise endeavor that burned the bottom layer of beans while leaving those on top cold. When bedtime came, we unrolled my father's old sleeping bags to find them stinking of damp mold. The odor was so ④<u>faint</u> that even my father gave up. We packed the tent, got in the car, and drove home.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① swell=붓다 ② dinner=저녁 ③ beans=콩 ④ faint=희미한 → overpowering(압도적인)
det.analysis:
① swell: 이마가 '붓다' — 적절
② dinner: '저녁거리'를 낚시로 — 적절
③ beans: 콩 통조림 — 적절
④ faint: 냄새가 '희미한'데 아버지조차 포기했다? 포기할 정도면 압도적으로 강한(overpowering) 냄새여야 함 ←정답
det.tip: so ___ that even my father gave up → faint(희미한)이면 포기 이유가 안 됨. overpowering(압도적)

questions.passage: The Venus flytrap, a ①<u>meat-eating</u> plant, has a pair of leaves that act as jaws and a stomach. If an insect ②<u>touches</u> the trigger hairs on the surface of these leaves, the leaves close, trapping the insect. Amazingly, a recent experiment showed that the Venus flytrap knew how many times its trigger hairs were touched and could even count the time between these stimuli. The trap closed only if the plant ③<u>ignored</u> two stimuli within a 20 second time span. Once 20 seconds passed, the process was reset. In addition, more than three stimuli were required for the plant to begin producing the enzymes that ④<u>digest</u> the trapped insect. Thanks to this process, the Venus flytrap doesn't make meaningless efforts trying to trap and digest raindrops or fallen leaves.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 정답 ③ ignored → sensed: 덫은 자극을 '감지했을' 때만 닫히므로 '무시했다(ignored)'는 정반대예요.
det.analysis:
① meat-eating: 파리지옥은 곤충을 잡아먹는 '육식성(meat-eating)' 식물이 맞아요. (적절)

② touches: 곤충이 감각모를 '건드리면(touches)' 잎이 닫힌다는 흐름이 맞아요. (적절)

③ ignored → sensed ←정답: 'The trap closed only if the plant ______ two stimuli(그 식물이 두 개의 자극을 ~했을 때만 덫이 닫혔다)'예요. 덫이 닫히려면 자극을 '감지해야(sensed)' 하는데, ignored(무시했다)를 쓰면 정반대 뜻이 돼요. (sense: 감지하다)

④ digest: 효소가 잡힌 곤충을 '소화한다(digest)'는 흐름이 맞아요. (적절)
det.tip: 덫이 닫히는 조건 = 자극을 감지함(sensed). 무시(ignored)와 반대예요.

questions.stem:
다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 [조건]의 단어를 모두 사용하여 영어로 문장을 완성하시오. (6단어)

det.analysis:

최종: we / cooked / a / can / of / beans (6단어).

If an insect touches the trigger hairs on the surface of these leaves, the leaves close, trapping the insect. questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 빈칸을 완성하시오. (9단어, 영어로)
'세 번보다 많은 자극이 그 식물에게 요구되었다'
[조건] (1) for, more, plant, required, stimuli, than, the, three, were를 모두 사용
(2) 9단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: '세 번보다 많은 자극이 요구되었다'는 수동태(be동사 + 과거분사) 문장이에요.
det.analysis:
본문 문장: 'In addition, __________ to begin producing the enzymes...(게다가, 효소를 만들기 시작하려면 ~이 요구되었다)'예요.

① 주어부: '세 번보다 많은 자극' = more than three stimuli.

② 동사부: '요구되었다'는 자극이 요구를 '당하는' 것이라 수동태로 써요 → were required(be동사 were + 과거분사 required). 주어 stimuli가 복수라 was가 아니라 were예요.

③ '그 식물에게'는 for the plant로 붙여요.

④ 순서대로 이으면 more than three stimuli were required for the plant (9단어)예요.
det.tip: 수동태 = be동사 + 과거분사. 복수 주어(stimuli) → were required.

questions.wa: more than three stimuli were required for the plant
accept: more than three stimuli were required for the plant

questions.passage: The "Rat Park" was an experiment conducted by a psychologist in the late 1970s. It was used to show that a social community can be more powerful than drugs. In the experiment, __________, one containing plain water and the other containing water with morphine added to it. The psychologist found that rats kept together drank much less of the morphine water than rats kept alone. He concluded that addictive qualities aren't the only thing that promotes drug use. The social and environmental conditions of the individual also play an important role. This seems to apply to humans as well as rats. People who are lonely and isolated are more likely to become addicted to drugs. But if these conditions are improved, their chances of breaking the addiction increase. This means that social recovery could someday become a treatment for drug addiction.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 빈칸을 완성하시오. (8단어) (영어로)
'쥐들에게 두 개의 물병 사이에서 선택권이 주어졌다'
[조건] (1) a, between, bottles, choice, given, rats, two, were를 모두 사용
(2) 8단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: rats were given a choice between two bottles = 쥐들에게 두 물병 사이의 선택권이 주어졌다
det.analysis: 수동태 be given(주어지다)을 이용해요. 주어 rats + were given(주어졌다) + a choice(선택권) + between two bottles(두 병 사이의). 'A에게 B가 주어지다'는 A were given B
det.tip: were given = 주어졌다(수동태). rats were given a choice = 쥐들에게 선택권이 주어졌다

questions.wa: rats were given a choice between two bottles
accept: rats were given a choice between two bottles

questions.passage: "Negative pressure" refers to a situation in which the pressure of an enclosed area is lower than that of the surrounding area. If the barrier between these two areas breaks, __________ will immediately flow into the low-pressure area. For example, undersea pipes used to transport oil are in a state of negative pressure; therefore, any break in the pipeline will cause it to fill with ocean water. This is much better than the opposite scenario, in which oil would be released into the ocean. However, negative pressure is not always beneficial, such as in the case of pipes carrying drinking water to a city. If these municipal waterlines are damaged, they can potentially suck in contaminated groundwater, which would then enter the water supply. For this reason, a system of gauges and valves is used to adjust and control their pressure.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 빈칸을 완성하시오. (영어로)
'고압 영역에 있는 모든 물질'
[조건] (1) any, area, high-pressure, in, substances, the를 모두 사용
(2) 6단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: any substances in the high-pressure area = 고압 영역에 있는 모든 물질
det.analysis:
핵심은 '어떤 물질(any substances)'을 먼저 쓰고, 그 물질이 있는 장소를 전치사구 'in the high-pressure area(고압 영역 안에)'로 뒤에서 꾸며 주는 거예요.

① any substances(모든 물질) → ② in(~안에) → ③ the high-pressure area(그 고압 영역).

완성: any substances in the high-pressure area (6단어)
det.tip: 명사(any substances) + 전치사구(in the high-pressure area)로 장소를 뒤에서 수식

questions.wa: any substances in the high-pressure area
accept: any substances in the high-pressure area

questions.passage: If astronauts travel to Mars in the near future, the journey will probably take years. Therefore, __________ will be a major challenge. Scientists are now looking for ways to allow astronauts to extend their food supply by growing crops. Seeds take up less storage space than packaged meals, and astronauts can plant them once they reach Mars. NASA is already conducting experiments to find out what might grow on Mars. The soil on Mars is made up mostly of crushed rocks, so it has few or no nutrients. In a test, NASA planted lettuce in crushed volcanic rock from Hawaii, which also contains few nutrients. The lettuce took a long time to grow, but it tasted normal. Because this test was a success, NASA now plans to find out how long other vegetables would take to grow on Mars.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 빈칸을 완성하시오. (영어로)
'우주비행사들에게 충분히 먹을 것을 제공하는 것'
[조건] (1) astronauts, eat, enough, providing, the, to, with를 모두 사용
(2) 7단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: providing the astronauts with enough to eat = 우주비행사들에게 충분히 먹을 것을 제공하는 것
det.analysis:
동명사 providing으로 시작하는 주어구입니다. 'provide A with B(A에게 B를 제공하다)' 구문을 씁니다.

주어 역할이라 동명사 providing → 목적어 the astronauts → with enough to eat(충분히 먹을 것을) 순서로 배열합니다.
det.tip: provide + 사람(the astronauts) + with + 사물(enough to eat). 주어라서 providing(동명사)

questions.wa: providing the astronauts with enough to eat
accept: providing the astronauts with enough to eat
